_README: Visa-free-but-K-ETA-required guide: Thailand → Korea. Visa-free 90 days, but Thailand is NOT on the temporary K-ETA exemption list, so K-ETA must be applied for. Numbers grounded in facts.json (visa-thailand-free, keta-fee-validity).
metaTitle: Thailand to Korea: Do You Need a Visa? (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Do Thai passport holders need a visa for South Korea? No — visa-free for up to 90 days. But you DO need K-ETA (₩10,000, valid 3 years): Thailand isn't on the K-ETA waiver list. Apply early — step-by-step entry guide inside.

verdict.headline: No tourist visa needed — but you must apply for K-ETA.
verdict.sub: Thai passports are visa-free for short tourism, so there's no visa to apply for. But Thailand is not on the K-ETA waiver list, so you must get a K-ETA before you fly. With a valid K-ETA you're then exempt from the e-Arrival Card.

highlights.title: No visa for up to 90 days
highlights.body: Under the Korea–Thailand visa-waiver agreement, Thai passport holders enter Korea visa-free for short-term tourism and can stay up to 90 days. There is no tourist-visa application to file.

highlights.title: But you DO need K-ETA
highlights.body: Thailand is not among the 22 countries/regions on the temporary K-ETA waiver, so you must apply for K-ETA before boarding. It costs KRW 10,000 (about US$8), is valid for 3 years with multiple entries, and is applied for only at the official site k-eta.go.kr.

highlights.title: Apply early — approval isn't automatic
highlights.body: A K-ETA (and the final immigration decision on arrival) is not guaranteed. Apply early, answer honestly, and keep your trip genuinely for tourism — carry your return ticket, hotel booking and proof of funds. If you hold a valid K-ETA you're exempt from the e-Arrival Card.

items.title: Confirm you're visa-free
items.detail: Thai passports enter Korea visa-free for short tourism (up to 90 days) — there's no tourist visa to apply for.

items.title: Apply for K-ETA (required)
items.detail: Apply at the official site k-eta.go.kr at least 72 hours before boarding. The fee is KRW 10,000, valid 3 years with multiple entries. Beware copycat sites that charge extra — only k-eta.go.kr is official.

items.title: Prepare your travel proof
items.detail: Have your return/onward ticket, confirmed accommodation, and proof of funds ready. Approval and entry aren't automatic, so genuine tourism documents help.

items.title: At immigration
items.detail: With a valid K-ETA you don't file the e-Arrival Card. Show your passport and travel documents at arrival; fingerprints and a photo may be taken. Keep it tourism — no paid work on visa-free entry.

items.q: Do Thai passport holders need a visa for Korea?
items.a: No — for short-term tourism, Thai passport holders enter Korea visa-free and can stay up to 90 days. You do not apply for any tourist visa.
